crossing supervisor Listen Share on Facebook Share on Twitter Print Content components School crossing supervisors have a much-valued role in Boroondara. On an average school day in Boroondara, they help 9,266 pedestrians to cross the street while 74,426 motor vehicles use our roads during school crossing times. We are always looking for school crossing supervisors. If you are friendly, reliable and flexible, this role is for you. What does a school crossing supervisor do? This paid position gives you the opportunity to get involved in your community and improve road safety for children, people with a disability and the general public who use our 114 school crossings. School crossing supervisors: • work part-time Monday to Friday, from 8 am to 9 am and from 3 pm to 4 pm, during the school term • play an important role in educating children with ‘Stop, Look and Listen’ instructions • are responsible for reporting any road hazards or potential risks • help to encourage active and independent travel. About you We are looking for people aged 18 and older who: • can attend shifts at short notice • have their own reliable transport • are able to work across several locations • can complete the pre-employment medical and police checks. You will have access to a full training program before starting your role. Download the position description School Crossing Supervisor PD 144.04 KB [PDF] 23 November 2022 How to apply Learn more about this rewarding role by reading the position description above. Submit an online application through our Careers website . Attend an interview – meet with one of our Council Officers at Council, located at 8 Inglesby Road in Camberwell. Provide us with relevant employment documents – including your Working With Children Check, Police Check and evidence of your COVID-19 vaccination status. Complete a medical assessment. Apply to become a School Crossings Supervisor We are always recruiting new school crossing supervisors to help people to cross our roads safely at peak school times. Skip to Main Content Career Opportunities: Park Asset Specialist (15178) Requisition ID 15178 - Posted - Job Function (2) - Tenure Status (1) - Employment Status (1)  Job Description Print Preview Apply Save Job Email Job to Friend Return to List $73,273 to $78,901 (ongoing, full time, plus superannuation, 9 day fortnight) Build and maintain the parks and playgrounds that our community enjoys every day Work outdoors across some of Melbourne's most valued parks and reserves The Role Reporting to the Parks Team Leader, the Park Asset Specialist plays an important role in maintaining the safety, functionality and presentation of Council's playgrounds, park furniture and associated infrastructure. Based at Kew Depot and working across the municipality, this hands-on role is responsible for delivering maintenance and repair services that ensure our parks and open spaces remain safe, attractive and welcoming for the community. You will undertake a variety of maintenance activities, inspections and repair works while working collaboratively with colleagues, contractors and members of the public. Key Responsibilities Carry out maintenance, repairs and minor construction works across playgrounds, park furniture and fence assets within Council's open spaces. Undertake routine playground inspections and audits to ensure compliance with relevant Australian Standards and identify any safety concerns. Arrange for hazards and defects to be repaired, replaced or made safe in a timely manner, ensuring community safety remains a priority. Plan and complete maintenance works while considering the horticultural amenity and presentation of park sites, leaving work areas clean and safe upon completion . About You You will bring practical experience in outdoor maintenance, construction, landscaping, carpentry or a related field, together with a strong commitment to safety and high-quality workmanship. You have experience installing, repairing and maintaining outdoor furniture, structures or timber assets and enjoy working in a physically active outdoor environment. You are self-motivated, organised and capable of managing your workload while responding to changing priorities. Your ability to work both independently and as part of a team, combined with strong communication skills, will enable you to build positive relationships with colleagues and the community. Qualifications or experience in carpentry, landscaping, welding, forklift operation or medium rigid vehicle operation will be highly regarded. For more information regarding the role, please refer to the attached position description. About Boroondara The City of Boroondara is home to some of Melbourne's most beautiful parks, playgrounds, gardens and open spaces. We are committed to creating a healthy, connected and sustainable community and delivering services that place our customers at the centre of everything we do. As one of Melbourne's most desirable municipalities, we take pride in maintaining high quality public spaces that support recreation, wellbeing and community connection. Working with us means contributing to assets and environments that are enjoyed by thousands of residents and visitors each year. Employment Requirements Applicants must hold unrestricted working rights in Australia, and those progressing through the selection process will need to complete a National Police Record Check, a Working with Children Check and relevant pre-employment medical assessments. How to Apply Please submit your application online via the 'Apply' button by 11.59pm, Sunday 23 August 2026. All applications must be made via the online portal; no applications direct to the hiring manager or from recruitment agencies will be considered. We are seeking skilled and experienced professional care workers who love supporting people to live independently in the community. We currently provide services in Mount Alexander Shire and Central Goldfields Shire. This is your opportunity to bring your passion and skills to be part of a professional and dedicated team providing high quality in-home support to frail older people and people with disabilities in our community. The role provides tailored services to help clients live healthy, independent and active lives through assistance with daily tasks and activities. Direct Care Worker Traineeship Opportunities: If you don’t already have a certificate III in Individual Support, you can also apply here for a Trainee Direct Care Worker position, to earn and learn on the job. Minimum Qualifications and Experience You must have, or be willing to obtain: Current Police Check Current Working with Children Check Triple vaccinated for COVID (2 doses plus a booster). Current Drivers license and roadworthy, registered and comprehensively insured vehicle for work travel Applicants must be able to work weekends. First Aid and CPR certificate will be gained though training and applied to the role as required If you have any queries or would like to discuss the role, the key contacts are: Sarah Newstead In Home Support Coordinator – East (03) 5471 1845 Talia Jenkin In Home Support Coordinator – West (03) 5471 1728 To apply for a Direct Care Worker or Direct Care Worker Trainee position, please provide a cover letter (no more than 2 pages) outlining why you are interested and the best candidate for this role, and your current resume. Additional information Mount Alexander Shire Council is committed to providing a safe, inclusive, and respectful workplace. We are an equal opportunity employer and are committed to child safety with zero tolerance for child abuse. We value a diverse workforce and encourage applicants from all cultures, sexual orientations, gender identities and backgrounds. Applicants can expect that the recruitment process will include interviewing, reference checks and criminal history checks. Some positions will also be required to provide a Working with Children Check, and medical assessments including drug and alcohol testing may be undertaken. For more information on the recruitment process, please download the Candidate information document from our website.
